280.d:
In the 12th month of 265 Sima Yan accepted the abdication of Wei, naming his dynasty Jin, with its capital at Luoyang. In the winter of 279 Jin attacked Wu along six routes; in the 2nd month of 280 Wang Jun (王濬) burned through the iron chains that Wu had stretched across the Yangtze and sailed downstream, and in the 3rd month his towered warships reached Shitou City. Sun Hao came out with his hands bound and surrendered, Wu fell, and Jin gained Wu's four provinces, forty-three commanderies and 523,000 households, ending nearly a century of division that had begun with the Yellow Turban rising.
Jin divided the realm into nineteen provinces. On the northern frontier the Xianbei tribes lived scattered on both sides of the frontier alongside the Xiongnu, Qiang and Hu; in the northeast lay Buyeo and Goguryeo; the states of the Western Regions nominally submitted to Jin, and in the south Linyi repeatedly raided Rinan. In the far west Sasanian Persia and Rome (Daqin) faced each other across the Euphrates, and in India remnants of the Kushans lingered.

289.t: Princes sent to regional posts · the Murong submit to Jin
289.d:
The Taikang era was a time of peace: Emperor Wu of Jin disbanded the provincial and commandery troops and introduced the zhantian and ketian land system. In 285 Murong Hui of the Xianbei crushed Buyeo in the east and its king Yilü killed himself; the next year He Kan, Jin Colonel of the Eastern Peoples, helped his son Yiluo restore the state. In 289 Murong Hui submitted to Jin and moved to Qingshan near Tuhe. In the 11th month Emperor Wu posted his sons to key regions: Sima Jian, Prince of Qin, commanded Guanzhong; Sima Wei, Prince of Chu, Jing Province; Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan, Yang and Jiang; and Sima Liang, Prince of Runan, went out as Grand Marshal to Xuchang.
The Tuoba Xianbei held Shengle in Dingxiang, the Duan and the Yuwen lived beyond the frontier of Liaoxi, and the Chile (Gaoche) tribes roamed north of the Gobi. In Rome Diocletian was on the throne, and in 287 he installed Tiridates III as King of Armenia.

296.t: War of the Eight Princes begins · Qi Wannian rises
296.d:
Emperor Wu died in 290 and Emperor Hui took the throne, with Yang Jun, father of the empress dowager, as regent. In 291 Empress Jia Nanfeng first used Sima Wei, Prince of Chu, to execute Yang Jun and kill Sima Liang, Prince of Runan, then executed Sima Wei for forging an edict, taking sole control of the court — the beginning of the War of the Eight Princes. In 294 Hao San of the Xiongnu rose in Shangdang; in 296 his younger brother Hao Duyuan rebelled against Jin together with the Malan Qiang and the Lushui Hu of Pingyi and Beidi, and the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong provinces made the Di chieftain Qi Wannian emperor; with seventy thousand men he camped at Liangshan, and Guanzhong was in turmoil. The same year Yang Maosou, a Di from Lüeyang, led his people back to Chouchi and styled himself General Who Supports the State and Worthy King of the Right.
In 295 the Tuoba Xianbei split into three: Luguan lived north of Shanggu, Yituo at Canhe Slope in Dai Commandery, and Yilu at Shengle in Dingxiang. In 294 Murong Hui moved to Daji City and taught his people farming and sericulture.

300.t: Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, seizes power
300.d:
In the 1st month of 297 Zhou Chu was ordered to attack Qi Wannian at Liumo with five thousand men and died fighting hard; in the 1st month of 299 Meng Guan crushed the Di and Qiang at Zhongting and captured Qi Wannian alive, and Guanzhong was pacified. Jiang Tong, Librarian to the Crown Prince, wrote his Essay on Moving the Rong, urging that the Di and Qiang of Guanzhong and the Xiongnu of Bing Province be moved back to their old lands; the court could not act on it. In the 12th month of 299 Empress Jia falsely accused the crown prince Sima Yu of plotting rebellion and had him reduced to a commoner.
In the 3rd month of 300 Empress Jia killed Sima Yu; in the 4th month Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, and Sun Xiu forged an edict, deposed and killed Empress Jia, executed Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, and Sima Lun made himself Chancellor of State and ruled alone; in the 8th month Sima Yun, Prince of Huainan, rose against him and was defeated and killed. In the winter Zhao Xin, Inspector of Yi Province, rebelled at Chengdu, winning over Li Te and his brothers, leaders of the refugees from six commanderies of Lüeyang and Tianshui who had flooded into Ba-Shu.

301.t: Three princes move against Sima Lun · Li Te rises
301.d:
In the 1st month Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, usurped the throne and moved Emperor Hui to Jinyong City. In the 3rd month Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, rose at Xuchang, Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, at Ye, and Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, at Chang'an against Sima Lun, and Sima Ai, Prince of Changshan, joined them; in the 4th month Sima Lun was defeated and ordered to take his own life, Emperor Hui was restored, and Sima Jiong became regent as Grand Marshal, while Sima Ying and Sima Yong returned to their own posts — the three princes divided Luoyang, Hebei and Guanzhong between them.
In the 1st month Li Te and his brothers attacked and killed Zhao Xin; the court sent Luo Shang as Inspector of Yi Province, and he pressed the refugees to go home; in the 10th month Li Te rose in arms at Mianzhu, and more than a hundred thousand refugees joined him. The same year Zhang Gui became Inspector of Liang Province, holding Hexi securely and taking in refugees from the Central Plain.

302.t: Sima Ai, Prince of Changsha, kills Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi
302.d:
As regent, Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi, grew arrogant and high-handed, building great mansions and failing to attend on the emperor. Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, and Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, agreed to move against him, but in the 12th month Sima Ai, Prince of Changsha, struck first in Luoyang, leading his followers against Sima Jiong's residence; after three days of fierce fighting he beheaded Sima Jiong and more than two thousand of his partisans and took charge of the court, while Sima Ying and Sima Yong still pulled the strings from outside.
In Ba-Shu Li Te defeated Luo Shang again and again, took Deyang, styled himself Governor of Yi Province and Grand General, and proclaimed the era name Jianchu; Luo Shang fell back to hold Chengdu.

303.t: Zhang Chang rises · Li Xiong enters Chengdu
303.d:
In the 1st month Li Te broke into the Lesser City of Chengdu, but in the 3rd month he was killed in a night attack by Luo Shang; his younger brother Li Liu and his son Li Xiong took over the refugees; in the 9th month Li Liu died of illness, and in the intercalary 12th month Li Xiong took Chengdu, and Luo Shang fled to Jiangyang.
In the 5th month Zhang Chang of the Yiyang tribes rose at Jiangxia and made Qiu Shen Son of Heaven; within a month much of the five provinces of Jing, Jiang, Yang, Xu and Yu had fallen. Liu Hong, Inspector of Jing Province, sent Tao Kan, who crushed Zhang Chang, but his general Shi Bing still held Yang Province and Linhuai.
In the 8th month Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, and Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, joined forces against Sima Ai, Prince of Changsha, with Zhang Fang advancing on Luoyang from Guanzhong and Lu Ji from Hebei; in the 10th month Lu Ji was routed at Qilijian and killed by Sima Ying, while Sima Ai held Luoyang.

304.t: Battle of Dangyin · Han and Cheng founded side by side
304.d:
In the 1st month Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, seized Sima Ai, Prince of Changsha, who was burned to death by Zhang Fang, and Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, as Chancellor and Imperial Younger Brother and heir, directed the court from Ye. In the 7th month Sima Yue took Emperor Hui north on campaign and was routed by Sima Ying's army at Dangyin; the emperor was struck in the face by three arrows and carried captive into Ye, Ji Shao died shielding him with his body, and Sima Yue fled back to Donghai. In the 8th month Wang Jun, Area Commander of You Province, with Duan Xianbei and Wuhuan shock cavalry, joined Sima Teng, Inspector of Bing Province, in attacking Ye, and Sima Ying fled to Luoyang with the emperor; in the 11th month Zhang Fang carried off the emperor and Sima Ying west to Chang'an, and the court passed wholly to Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian.
In the 10th month Liu Yuan, Worthy King of the Left of the Xiongnu, proclaimed himself King of Han at Zuoguo City near Lishi (Han Zhao), and Li Xiong proclaimed himself King of Chengdu at Chengdu (Cheng Han): in the same year two breakaway regimes appeared, in the north and in Ba-Shu. Chen Min destroyed Shi Bing, and Jiangdong returned to Jin.

305.t: Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, takes up arms · Chen Min holds Jiangdong
305.d:
In the 7th month Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, sent proclamations throughout the east and rose in arms in the name of bringing back the Son of Heaven; Sima Xiao, Prince of Fanyang, Wang Jun of You Province and Sima Teng of Bing Province answered his call. Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, made Liu Qiao Inspector of Yu Province to oppose them; in the 10th month Liu Qiao took Xuchang by surprise and drove out Sima Xiao, who fled north to Hebei and held Ji Province. Gongshi Fan, Ji Sang and Shi Le, old officers of Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, rose in Zhao and Wei in the name of restoring him.
In the 12th month Chen Min, Chancellor of Guangling, rebelled at Liyang, styled himself Duke of Chu and Commander of all Armies of Jiangdong, drove out the Inspector of Yang Province and held the whole of Jiangdong. Liu Yuan, King of Han, fought Sima Teng for Bing Province; Lishi suffered a great famine, and Liu Yuan moved south to Liting.

306.t: Emperor Hui returns east · War of the Eight Princes ends
306.d:
In the 1st month Sima Xiao, Prince of Fanyang, and Wang Jun crushed Liu Qiao; Wang Jun's general Qi Hong advanced west with Xianbei shock cavalry, broke into Chang'an in the 5th month and plundered it, killing more than twenty thousand people, and Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, fled into the Taibai Mountains; in the 6th month Emperor Hui returned east to Luoyang and Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, took charge of the government. In the 10th month Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, was strangled; in the 11th month Emperor Hui died after eating poisoned cakes, and the Imperial Younger Brother Sima Chi took the throne (Emperor Huai); in the 12th month Sima Yong, summoned to court, was killed on the way by Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang. The War of the Eight Princes was over; of the eight, only Sima Yue survived.
In the 6th month Li Xiong proclaimed himself emperor at Chengdu, naming his state Great Cheng. Sima Teng, Prince of Dongyan, moved his post to Ye, Liu Kun succeeded him as Inspector of Bing Province, and the Han army already held most of Bing Province.

307.t: Sima Rui takes post at Jianye · Ji Sang and Shi Le sack Ye
307.d:
In the 2nd month Chen Min's officers Gan Zhuo, Gu Rong and others turned against him, Chen Min was defeated and killed, and Jiangdong returned to Jin. In the 5th month Ji Sang and Shi Le, avenging Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, took Ye, killed Sima Teng and burned the palaces of Ye; Gou Xi, Inspector of Yan Province, defeated them again and again, Ji Sang was killed, and Shi Le went over to Liu Yuan, King of Han. In the 7th month Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, gave Sima Rui, Prince of Langya, command over the armies of Yang Province; in the 9th month Sima Rui crossed the Yangtze to take up his post at Jianye, with Wang Dao as his chief adviser, and won over the great families of Jiangdong.
The same year Wang Mi rose in Qing and Xu, and Liu Kun reached Jinyang, gathered the displaced, allied himself with the Tuoba in the north, and held out against Liu Yuan. Sima Yue went out to Xuchang.

308.t: Liu Yuan proclaims himself emperor · Wang Mi raids Luoyang
308.d: In the 1st month the Han army took Pingyang and the counties of Hedong, and Liu Yuan held the Fen valley; Shi Le and Wang Mi ranged across Ji, Yan and Yu provinces, laying waste wherever they went. In the 5th month Wang Mi pushed from Xuchang into the outskirts of Luoyang and burned the Jianchun Gate, but was driven off by Wang Bing, a general of Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, and went over to Liu Yuan. In the 10th month Liu Yuan took the imperial throne at Puzi, proclaimed the era name Yongfeng, and sent Liu Cong, Liu Yao, Shi Le and Wang Mi south along separate routes. Murong Hui styled himself Grand Chanyu of the Xianbei.

309.t: Han makes Pingyang its capital · two attacks on Luoyang
309.d: In the 1st month Liu Yuan moved his capital to Pingyang. In the 3rd month Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, entered Luoyang and executed Wang Yan (王延), Miao Bo and other confidants of Emperor Huai, and the government passed wholly to his headquarters. In the 7th month the Han generals Liu Cong and Wang Mi took Huguan, and the Jin Administrator of Shangdang surrendered to Han; in the 8th month Liu Cong attacked Luoyang, but Yuan Yan, Administrator of Hongnong, feigned surrender and attacked by night, and the Han army fell back; in the 10th month Liu Cong attacked Luoyang again, besieged it for a long time without success, and withdrew. Shi Le took the commanderies and counties of Ji Province one after another, and Hebei lay in ruins.

310.t: Liu Cong takes the throne · the Tuoba gain the lands north of the Gouzhu Defile
310.d:
In the 7th month Liu Yuan died of illness; the crown prince Liu He tried to do away with his brothers and was himself killed by Liu Cong, Prince of Chu, who took the throne. Shi Le crossed the Yellow River southward, raided Xiangcheng and Wan, and fought his way through the Jiang–Han region; Wang Ru, a leader of refugees from Guanzhong, rose at Wan, his following grew to forty or fifty thousand, and he advanced to besiege Xiangyang.
Tuoba Yilu helped Liu Kun crush Liu Hu of the Tiefu Xiongnu and the Bai Xianbei, and Liu Hu fled to Shuofang. Jin made Yilu Duke of Dai and gave him five counties north of the Gouzhu Defile — Mayi, Yinguan, Loufan, Fanzhi and Guo. Luoyang was starving and hard-pressed; in the 11th month Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, went out with forty thousand armored men to garrison Xiangcheng, leaving the court empty.

311.d:
In the 3rd month Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, died of illness at Xiangcheng; his army of more than a hundred thousand was led back east by Wang Yan (王衍), and in the 4th month it was overtaken by Shi Le's cavalry at Ningping City in Ku County, surrounded and wiped out, and Wang Yan and others were killed. In the 6th month Liu Yao, Wang Mi and Shi Le took Luoyang, let their troops burn and loot, and killed more than thirty thousand princes, officials and townspeople; Emperor Huai was captured and sent to Pingyang — the Disaster of Yongjia. In the 8th month Liu Yao took Chang'an and Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang, was killed. In the 9th month Shi Le captured Gou Xi at Mengcheng, and in the 10th month he invited Wang Mi to a banquet at Jiwu, killed him and absorbed his army; Wang Mi's general Cao Ni held Qing Province.
Sima Rui destroyed Hua Yi, Inspector of Jiang Province, and Zhou Fu, Area Commander of Yang Province, and held the middle and lower Yangtze. The refugees of Xiang Province chose Du Tao as their leader and rose at Changsha. The gentry and people of the Central Plain crossed south of the Yangtze one after another — "the flight of the caps and gowns to the south".

312.t: Shi Le holds Xiangguo · Jin retakes Chang'an
312.d: Shi Le camped at Gebei for three months; beset by incessant rain, famine and disease, he followed Zhang Bin's plan and went back north, and in the 7th month he occupied Xiangguo, which became his base for building up Hebei. In the 4th month Jia Ya, Administrator of Anding, and others joined forces, drove out Liu Yao and recovered Chang'an; in the 9th month Sima Ye, Prince of Qin, was welcomed into Chang'an and made crown prince. The Han general Liu Can seized Jinyang by surprise, and Liu Kun recovered it with troops borrowed from Tuoba Yilu. After Emperor Huai's capture, Wang Jun in You Province set up a crown prince of his own — serving Jin in name, acting for himself in fact. Wang Ru surrendered to Wang Dun.

313.t: Emperor Min takes the throne · Zu Ti crosses the Yangtze
313.d:
In the 1st month the Han ruler Liu Cong poisoned Emperor Huai at Pingyang; in the 4th month the crown prince Sima Ye took the throne at Chang'an (Emperor Min), made Sima Rui, Prince of Langya, Chancellor of the Left and Sima Bao, Prince of Nanyang, Chancellor of the Right, and ordered them to send troops from east and west of Shan, but neither Jiangdong nor Qin Province sent any. Shi Hu took the Three Terraces of Ye. In the 8th month Zu Ti, as General of Roused Might and Inspector of Yu Province, crossed the Yangtze on a northern expedition with over a hundred households of his retainers, striking his oar in midstream and swearing: "If I cannot clear the Central Plain and cross back, may I be like this great river!"
King Micheon of Goguryeo destroyed Lelang Commandery, ending more than four hundred years of the commandery rule of the Han, Wei and Jin on the Korean peninsula. Tao Kan defeated Du Tao again and again in Jing Province.

314.d: In the 3rd month Shi Le pretended that he wished to make Wang Jun emperor, broke into Ji City with light cavalry, captured Wang Jun and beheaded him at Xiangguo, burning his palace before returning; the commanders Shi Le left behind promptly surrendered to Duan Pidi of the Duan Xianbei, who held Ji as Jin Inspector of You Province. Goguryeo also took Daifang Commandery. In the 5th month Zhang Gui, Inspector of Liang Province, died, and his son Zhang Shi succeeded him, still following the Jin calendar. The Han ruler Liu Cong gave himself over to pleasure and banquets, made his son Liu Can Chancellor of State, and government fell into growing disorder.

315.t: Du Tao suppressed · the Tuoba ruler made King of Dai
315.d: Tao Kan, Zhou Fang and others put down Du Tao, and Jing and Xiang provinces returned to Jin; for his part Wang Dun was given command of six provinces — Jiang, Yang, Jing, Xiang, Jiao and Guang — and kept the post of Inspector of Jiang Province for himself, pushing Tao Kan out to be Inspector of Guang Province, and from then on he ruled the upper Yangtze as he pleased. In the 2nd month Jin raised Tuoba Yilu to King of Dai; he set up a bureaucracy, with Shengle as his northern capital and Pingcheng as his southern capital. The Han general Liu Yao raided Guanzhong year after year, and Chang'an was hard-pressed. Shi Le nibbled away at the commanderies and counties of Hebei.

316.t: Fall of Chang'an · end of Western Jin
316.d:
In the 3rd month Yilu, King of Dai, was killed by his son Liuxiu, and Dai fell into civil strife; Wei Xiong and Ji Dan fled to Bing Province with thirty thousand households of Chinese and Wuhuan, greatly strengthening Liu Kun, who soon lost them again. In the 8th month Liu Yao besieged Chang'an; inside the city a peck of grain cost two taels of gold, and people ate one another; in the 11th month Emperor Min rode out in a goat cart, stripped to the waist with a jade disc in his mouth, and surrendered; he was sent to Pingyang, and the Western Jin came to an end. In the 12th month Shi Le defeated Liu Kun at Leping, Bing Province passed to Shi Le, and Liu Kun fled north to Duan Pidi in You Province.
Now the only places north of the Yangtze that still kept the Jin calendar were isolated strongholds — Zhang Shi in Liang Province, Sima Bao in Qin Province, Duan Pidi in You Province, Shao Xu at Yanci in Leling, and Zu Ti; Sima Rui's circle in Jiangdong had become the Jin house's only support.

318.t: Eastern Jin founded · Jin Zhun's coup
318.d:
In the 3rd month of 317 Sima Rui, Prince of Langya, learning that Chang'an had fallen, took the title King of Jin at Jiankang; in the 12th month Emperor Min was murdered at Pingyang, and in the 3rd month of 318 Sima Rui ascended the imperial throne (Emperor Yuan) and the Eastern Jin was founded, with Wang Dao in charge at court and Wang Dun in charge in the provinces — as people said then, "the Wang and the Ma share the realm".
In the 7th month the Han ruler Liu Cong died of illness and the crown prince Liu Can took the throne; in the 8th month Jin Zhun, the empress's father, staged a coup, killed every man and woman of the Liu clan, and styled himself Heavenly King of Han. Liu Yao, guarding Chang'an, took the imperial throne in the 10th month, and Shi Le marched on Pingyang from Xiangguo; in the 12th month the Jin (靳) clan fell into strife, and Pingyang passed to Shi Le, who burned its palaces. Liu Yao made Shi Le Duke of Zhao; Shi Le was nominally his subject but had in fact made himself independent. Zhang Shi in Liang Province still used Emperor Min's era name Jianxing and did not follow edicts from Jiankang. Duan Pidi killed Liu Kun.

319.t: Former Zhao and Later Zhao split
319.era2: Former Zhao: Guangchu 2 · Later Zhao: King of Zhao 1
319.d:
In the 6th month Liu Yao moved his capital to Chang'an and renamed his state Zhao (Former Zhao); in the 11th month Shi Le proclaimed himself King of Zhao at Xiangguo and broke with Liu Yao (Later Zhao), with Zhang Bin as his chief adviser: in the north two Zhaos now faced each other, east and west.
Zu Ti advanced to the area of Yongqiu, held off the Later Zhao general Tao Bao, and took the city of Qiao. Murong Hui repelled an attack by Cui Bi, Inspector of Ping Province, together with Goguryeo, the Yuwen and the Duan, and took all of Liaodong. In the south Zhou Fang beheaded Du Zeng and pacified the area of Xiangyang. Sima Bao in Qin Province styled himself King of Jin, owing allegiance to neither the Former Zhao nor the Eastern Jin.

320.t: Zu Ti recovers the lands south of the Yellow River
320.era2: Former Zhao: Guangchu 3 · Later Zhao: King of Zhao 2
320.d: Zu Ti won over the masters of the fortified villages and encouraged farming and sericulture; filling cloth sacks with earth and passing them off as army grain, he shook the morale of the Later Zhao army, and much of the land south of the Yellow River returned to Jin. Many Later Zhao garrisons came over to him; Shi Le dared not raid southward and sent envoys asking to repair the tombs of Zu Ti's ancestors and to open trade. In the 2nd month Shi Hu of the Later Zhao captured Shao Xu, and Kong Chang took his eleven outlying camps; Duan Pidi hurried back from Ji and held Yanci with Shao Xu's son and nephews. In the 5th month Sima Bao in Qin Province was killed by his general Zhang Chun, and most of the commanderies of Longyou went over to the Former Zhao. In the 6th month Zhang Shi of the Former Liang was assassinated by his own men, and his younger brother Zhang Mao succeeded him.

322.era2: Former Zhao: Guangchu 5 · Later Zhao: King of Zhao 4
322.d: In the 9th month of 321 Zu Ti died of grief and illness at Yongqiu; his younger brother Zu Yue took over his army, and the cities of Henan gradually passed to the Later Zhao. The same year Shi Hu of the Later Zhao destroyed Duan Pidi, who was holding Yanci, and all of You Province passed to the Later Zhao; Tuoba Yulü of Dai was killed. In the 1st month of 322 Wang Dun rose at Wuchang and went down the Yangtze, claiming he would execute Liu Wei and Diao Xie; in the 3rd month he broke into Jiankang, Emperor Yuan gave in, and Wang Dun made himself Chancellor and returned to Wuchang to control the court from afar; in the intercalary 11th month Emperor Yuan died of grief and anger, and Emperor Ming took the throne. The Later Zhao seized the chance to take Xiangcheng, Chengfu and Qiao Commandery, and Zu Yue fell back to hold Shouchun.

324.era2: Former Zhao: Guangchu 7 · Later Zhao: King of Zhao 6
324.d: In 323 Shi Hu of the Later Zhao took Guanggu and killed Cao Ni, and Qing Province passed to the Later Zhao; Liu Yao of the Former Zhao put down Chen An in Longshang and led a great army to the Yellow River in person, Zhang Mao of the Former Liang submitted to the Former Zhao as a vassal, and the land south of the river (around Fuhan) passed to the Former Zhao. In 324 Wang Dun plotted rebellion again and sent his elder brother Wang Han as commander-in-chief against Jiankang; Emperor Ming led the armies in person to resist, and in the 7th month Wang Dun died of illness and the rebel army fell apart. The Former Zhao and the Later Zhao fought back and forth over the area of Luoyang and Henei.

328.t: Su Jun's rebellion · Battle of Luoyang
328.era2: Former Zhao: Guangchu 11 · Later Zhao: Taihe 1
328.d:
In 325 Shi Hu of the Later Zhao crushed Liu Yue of the Former Zhao at Luoyang, and the lands of Si, Yu, Xu and Yan provinces all passed to the Later Zhao. In 327 Yu Liang, now in charge of the government, summoned Su Jun, Administrator of Liyang, to court; Su Jun rose in arms together with Zu Yue at Shouchun, and in the 2nd month of 328 he broke into Jiankang, seized Emperor Cheng and let his troops plunder at will; Zu Yue lost Shouchun to the Later Zhao. Wen Jiao and Tao Kan brought the armies of Jing and Jiang down the Yangtze to punish him; in the 9th month Su Jun was killed in battle, but his remaining forces still held Shitou City.
In the north Liu Yao of the Former Zhao crushed Shi Hu at Gaohou and besieged Jinyong City at Luoyang; in the 12th month Shi Le crossed the Yellow River at the head of a great army, and Liu Yao, going out to fight drunk, was captured west of Luoyang.

329.d:
In the 1st month Liu Xi, crown prince of the Former Zhao, abandoned Chang'an and fled to Shanggui; in the 8th month Liu Yin led a counterattack on Chang'an and was crushed by Shi Hu, who took Shanggui in the 9th month and killed Liu Xi, Liu Yin and more than three thousand princes, ministers and officers: the Former Zhao fell, all of Guanlong passed to the Later Zhao, and the following year Shi Le proclaimed himself emperor. The Eastern Jin put down the remnants of Su Jun's forces in the 2nd month; the palaces of Jiankang lay in ruins, and Wang Dao argued strongly against moving the capital. Tao Kan commanded eight provinces including Jing and Jiang from Wuchang, and Xi Jian was stationed at Jingkou.
Zhang Jun of the Former Liang took advantage of the Former Zhao's fall to recover the lands south of the river; he had already set up Gaochang Commandery in 327, and the Chief Clerk of the Western Regions was still stationed at Haitou in Loulan. Yeyan, grandson of Murong Tuyuhun, made his grandfather's name the name of his state, holding the land west of the Tao and south of Qinghai (the Tuyuhun). In India the Gupta dynasty rose in Magadha (320).

335.t: Shi Hu moves to Ye · Cheng Han takes Ning Province
335.d:
In 330 Shi Le proclaimed himself emperor; the Later Zhao stretched from Liaoxi in the east to Longyou in the west and to the Huai and Han in the south, holding most of the north. Guo Jing took Xiangyang for a time, but the Jin general Huan Xuan (桓宣) recovered it in 332. In the 7th month of 333 Shi Le died of illness; the next year Shi Hu deposed and killed Shi Hong and took the throne himself, and in 335 he moved the capital to Ye, building palaces on a grand scale and conscripting women from among the people.
Li Shou of Cheng Han took Ning Province in 333, and all of Nanzhong passed to Cheng Han; Li Xiong died in 334 and the imperial clan turned on itself. Tao Kan of the Eastern Jin died in 334, and Yu Liang replaced him at Wuchang, commanding six provinces including Jiang, Jing and Yu. Murong Hui died in 333 and his son Murong Huang succeeded him, contending with his younger brother Murong Ren for Liaodong.

338.t: Former Yan claims kingship · Dai revived
338.d:
In 337 Murong Huang styled himself King of Yan (Former Yan). In 338 the Former Yan and the Later Zhao attacked the Duan together; Duan Liao fled defeated to the Miyun Mountains, and the Duan came to an end. The Later Zhao then turned its army on the Former Yan and besieged its capital, Daji City, for more than ten days; Murong Ke pursued the retreating Zhao army and took more than thirty thousand heads, and the Former Yan took over all the former Duan lands to the north.
The same year Tuoba Shiyijian became King of Dai, set up a bureaucracy and proclaimed the era name Jianguo, and Dai revived; Li Shou of Cheng Han killed Li Qi, took the throne himself and renamed the state Han. Yu Liang of the Eastern Jin planned a northern expedition that came to nothing.

346.t: Former Yan destroys the Yuwen · crushes Buyeo
346.d:
In 341 Murong Huang built Longcheng and moved his capital there the next year; he led his best troops in a surprise attack on Goguryeo, sacked Hwando, dug up the tomb of King Micheon, and returned with the king's mother and fifty thousand men and women as captives. In 344 Murong Huang campaigned in person against the Yuwen; Yuwen Yidougui fled far north of the Gobi and died, and the Yuwen came to an end. In the 1st month of 346 Murong Ke and others led cavalry in a surprise attack on Buyeo, capturing King Hyeon of Buyeo and more than fifty thousand of his people.
Yu Yi of the Eastern Jin died in 345, and Huan Wen became Inspector of Jing Province with command over six provinces including Jing and Si; in the 11th month he led his army up the Yangtze against Shu. In southwestern Korea Baekje rose to power under King Geunchogo.

347.d: In the 3rd month Huan Wen led his army straight for Chengdu and fought a decisive battle at Zuoqiao; the Jin vanguard faltered, but Huan Wen urged his men on to fight hard and crushed the Han army. Li Shi surrendered, Cheng Han fell, and Ba-Shu and Nanzhong returned to the Eastern Jin. Shi Hu of the Later Zhao sent Ma Qiu and others against the Former Liang, and Xie Ai of the Former Liang crushed them around Fuhan. Fan Wen, King of Linyi, took Rinan Commandery and killed its Administrator Xiahou Lan; thereafter the northern part of Rinan was long held by Linyi.

349.t: Death of Shi Hu · Later Zhao in chaos
349.d: In the 1st month Shi Hu took the imperial throne, and in the 4th month he died of illness; his sons turned on one another: Shi Zun killed Shi Shi and took the throne, then Ran Min killed Shi Zun and set up Shi Jian, and the Later Zhao fell into chaos. The Di chief Fu Hong and the Qiang chief Yao Yizhong held their followers at Fangtou and Shetou. Chu Pou of the Eastern Jin marched north and was defeated at Daibei; the Later Zhao Inspector of Yang Province surrendered Shouchun to Jin. Murong Huang of the Former Yan had died in 348, and his son Murong Jun succeeded him and readied his army to take the Central Plain.

350.t: Ran Min proclaims himself emperor · Yan armies march south
350.era2: Ran Wei: Yongxing 1 · Later Zhao: Yongning 1
350.d: In the 1st month Ran Min killed Shi Jian, and in the intercalary 2nd month he took the imperial throne, naming his state Wei (Ran Wei), and ordered the killing of the Hu: more than two hundred thousand died in and around Ye. Shi Zhi, Prince of Xinxing of the Later Zhao, proclaimed himself emperor at Xiangguo and fought Ran Min. In the 3rd month Murong Jun of the Former Yan took Ji City and moved his capital there. The Di chief Fu Hong was poisoned, and his son Fu Jian (苻健) led his people west into Guanzhong and took Chang'an in the 11th month. The Later Zhao commanders at Xuchang, Luoyang and elsewhere surrendered to Jin one after another, and Duan Kan, leading the remnants of the Duan, held Guanggu and styled himself King of Qi.

351.t: Former Qin founded · fall of Later Zhao
351.era2: Former Qin: Huangshi 1 · Ran Wei: Yongxing 2
351.d: In the 1st month Fu Jian (苻健) took the titles Heavenly King and Grand Chanyu at Chang'an, naming his state Great Qin (Former Qin). In the 4th month Shi Zhi of the Later Zhao was killed by his general Liu Xian, and the Later Zhao fell; Liu Xian promptly proclaimed himself emperor at Xiangguo and fought Ran Min. Ran Min campaigned east and west and was gravely weakened; Murong Ke of the Former Yan marched south and took Zhongshan, and Murong Ping took Bohai. Zhang Ping, the Later Zhao Inspector of Bing Province, held more than three hundred fortified strongholds there as a power in his own right; most of the Later Zhao commanders in Xu, Yan and Yu provinces surrendered to the Eastern Jin. Duan Kan acknowledged the Eastern Jin as his overlord.

352.t: Fall of Ran Wei · Former Yan ruler proclaims himself emperor
352.era2: Former Qin: Huangshi 2 · Former Yan: Yuanxi 1
352.d: In the 4th month Murong Ke crushed Ran Min at Liantai with chained cavalry, and Ran Min was captured and put to death; in the 8th month the Yan army took Ye, and Ran Wei fell. In the 11th month Murong Jun took the imperial throne at Ji City (Former Yan). Fu Jian (苻健) of the Former Qin proclaimed himself emperor and drove back Sima Xun, the Eastern Jin Inspector of Liang Province. Yin Hao of the Eastern Jin was ordered north, with the Qiang commander Yao Xiang as his vanguard camped at Qiao; Xie Shang obtained the imperial seal from the remnants of Ran Wei and sent it back to Jiankang.

354.t: Huan Wen's northern expedition against Former Qin
354.era2: Former Qin: Huangshi 4 · Former Yan: Yuanxi 3
354.d: In 353 Yin Hao marched north, but his vanguard under Yao Xiang turned against him; routed at Shansang, Yin Hao was reduced to a commoner, and from then on Huan Wen alone controlled the Eastern Jin's armies. In the 2nd month of 354 Huan Wen set out from Jiangling with forty thousand foot and horse, entered Guanzhong by the Wu Pass, crushed the Qin army at Lantian and advanced to Bashang; the elders of Guanzhong met him on the road with oxen and wine, sighing, "We never thought we would see the imperial army again." But Fu Jian (苻健) cleared the countryside and held his walls, the Jin army ran short of food, and after a setback at Bailuyuan in the 6th month it withdrew. Zhang Zuo of the Former Liang usurped the throne and proclaimed himself emperor, no longer acknowledging Jin.

356.era2: Former Qin: Shouguang 2 · Former Yan: Yuanxi 5
356.d: In the 8th month Huan Wen launched his second northern expedition, crushed Yao Xiang on the north bank of the Yi River and recovered Luoyang; he restored the tombs of the Western Jin emperors and petitioned for the capital to return to Luoyang, but the court did not respond. Yao Xiang fled west into Guanzhong. In the 11th month Murong Ke of the Former Yan took Guanggu, Duan Kan surrendered, and Qing Province passed to Yan. Fu Sheng, who had taken the throne of the Former Qin, was cruel and murderous. Zhang Zuo of the Former Liang was killed, and Zhang Xuanjing, who succeeded him, again acknowledged the Jin calendar.

357.t: Fu Jian takes the throne · Former Yan moves to Ye
357.era2: Former Qin: Yongxing 1 · Former Yan: Guangshou 1
357.d: In the 5th month Yao Xiang attacked Guanzhong and was killed at Sanyuan by Fu Huangmei and Deng Qiang of the Former Qin; his younger brother Yao Chang led their followers in surrender to Qin. In the 6th month Fu Jian (苻坚) killed the tyrant Fu Sheng and took the throne himself as Heavenly King of Great Qin; he employed Wang Meng to reform the administration and curb the great families, and the power of the Former Qin grew day by day. In the 11th month the Former Yan moved its capital to Ye. In southeastern Korea Saro united the states of Jinhan under King Naemul (Silla).

360.t: Death of Murong Jun · Yan takes the lands south of the Yellow River
360.era2: Former Qin: Ganlu 2 · Former Yan: Jianxi 1
360.d: Zhang Ping, who held Bing Province, submitted first to Yan and then to Qin, and after 358 most of Bing Province belonged to the Former Yan. In 359 Xie Wan of the Eastern Jin marched north, and his army broke up at Shouchun without fighting; the Former Yan seized the chance to take Xuchang, Yingchuan, Qiao and Pei, and north of the Huai the Eastern Jin kept only the isolated city of Luoyang. In the 1st month of 360 Murong Jun died of illness; his son Murong Wei took the throne, with the Grand Steward Murong Ke as regent. Wang Meng governed the Former Qin, and "the army was strong and the state rich, close to an age of peace".

365.era2: Former Qin: Jianyuan 1 · Former Yan: Jianxi 6
365.d:
In 362 Lü Hu of the Former Yan attacked Luoyang, and Huan Wen sent Deng Xia hurrying to its rescue; in 364 Murong Ke besieged it in person with a great army, and in the 3rd month of 365 he took Luoyang; its commander Shen Jin refused to yield and was killed, and the Yan army went on to overrun the Xiao–Mian area. Emperor Ai of the Eastern Jin trusted alchemists and fell ill from taking elixirs, and Huan Wen moved his seat to Gushu, controlling the court from afar. The Former Qin put down the rebellion of Liu Weichen and Cao Gu of the Xiongnu.
In the far west the Roman emperor Julian marched east against Persia in 363 and was killed near Ctesiphon; his successor Jovian ceded Nisibis to make peace. The Kidarites replaced the Kushans and held Tokharistan and Gandhara.

369.era2: Former Qin: Jianyuan 5 · Former Yan: Jianxi 10
369.d: In the 4th month Huan Wen launched his third northern expedition, setting out from Gushu with fifty thousand foot and horse; he cut a channel through the Juye Marsh to lead the Wen into the Ji, and his fleet reached Fangtou. The Former Yan was terrified, and Murong Wei asked the Former Qin for help, promising it the land west of Hulao. In the 9th month the Yan general Murong Chui held firm and cut the Jin supply line; Huan Wen burned his boats, abandoned his baggage and withdrew overland, and at Xiangyi he was ambushed by Murong Chui and Murong De, losing more than thirty thousand men. In the 10th month Yuan Zhen, Inspector of Yu Province, surrendered Shouchun to Yan. Murong Chui, whose merit had made him enemies, fled to the Former Qin in the 11th month.

370.d: The Former Yan refused to hand over the land west of Hulao, and the Former Qin attacked Yan with Wang Meng in command, taking Luoyang in the 1st month; in the 9th month Wang Meng took Jinyang, in the 10th month he crushed the three hundred thousand Yan troops under Murong Ping at Luchuan, and in the 11th month he took Ye; Murong Wei fled and was captured, the Former Yan fell, and its 157 commanderies and nearly ten million people all passed to the Former Qin. King Geunchogo of Baekje campaigned south against the remnants of Mahan and took all of the southwest of the peninsula.

371.t: Former Qin conquers Chouchi · Huan Wen deposes the emperor
371.d: In the 1st month Huan Wen took Shouchun and executed Yuan Jin. In the 4th month the Former Qin destroyed Yang Zuan of Chouchi, and the Qifu of the Longxi Xianbei and the Tuyuhun submitted to it in turn. In the 11th month Huan Wen deposed the emperor Sima Yi (司马奕), reducing him to Prince of Donghai, and set up Sima Yu (Emperor Jianwen), planning to take the throne himself. King Geunchogo of Baekje attacked the Goguryeo city of Pyongyang to the north, and King Gogugwon of Goguryeo was killed by a stray arrow.

373.t: Former Qin takes Liang and Yi provinces
373.d: Emperor Jianwen died in 372 and Emperor Xiaowu took the throne. In the 7th month of 373 Huan Wen died of illness without having usurped the throne, and Xie An and Wang Tanzhi took charge of the government; Huan Chong later gave up Yang Province and went out to Jing Province. From the 9th to the 11th month Wang Tong, Yang An and other Former Qin generals took Liang and Yi provinces; the Eastern Jin Inspector of Liang Province Yang Liang and Inspector of Yi Province Zhou Zhongsun fled defeated, and all of Ba-Shu passed to the Former Qin — "Qiong, Zuo and Yelang all submitted to Qin".

376.d:
In the 5th month the Former Qin sent Gou Chang, Liang Xi and others with 130,000 foot and horse against the Former Liang; in the 8th month Zhang Tianxi surrendered and the Former Liang fell. In the 10th month Fu Luo and others led an army of three hundred thousand against Dai; Shiyijian, King of Dai, ill, fled defeated and in the 12th month was killed by his son, and Dai fell; the Former Qin divided his people between Liu Kuren and Liu Weichen of the Xiongnu. The Former Qin had unified the north, and many states of the Western Regions sent envoys with tribute. Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin took personal control of the government with Xie An in charge, and Huan Chong had already given up Yang Province and gone out to garrison Jingkou.
In the far west the Huns moved west from beyond the Volga and crushed the Alans and the Ostrogoths, and the Gothic tribes crossed the Danube into Roman territory. In India Samudragupta of the Gupta dynasty conquered the states of the Ganges valley.

379.d: In the 2nd month of 378 Fu Pi of the Former Qin besieged Xiangyang with an army of 170,000; the Eastern Jin Inspector of Liang Province Zhu Xu held firm, and his mother, Lady Han, led her maids in building up a corner of the walls (the "Lady's Wall"); in the 2nd month of 379 the Area Protector Li Bohu opened the gates and surrendered to Qin, and Zhu Xu was captured. The Former Qin also took Weixing, Pengcheng, Huaiyin and Xuyi, and in the 5th month the Qin army surrounded the Jin army at San'e; Xie Xuan with the Northern Headquarters Army crushed the Qin generals Ju Nan and Peng Chao at Junchuan and recovered Huaiyin and Xuyi. From 377 Xie Xuan had been recruiting northern refugees at Guangling to form the Northern Headquarters Army.

383.d: In the 1st month Fu Jian sent Lü Guang with seventy thousand men west against the Western Regions. In the 8th month, ignoring the objections of his ministers, Fu Jian marched south against Jin in person with six hundred thousand foot and 270,000 horse, boasting that "if we throw our whips into the Yangtze we can stop its flow"; in the 10th month Fu Rong took Shouyang. In the 11th month Liu Laozhi made a night attack on Luojian with five thousand Northern Headquarters troops and beheaded the Qin general Liang Cheng; Xie Xuan, Xie Yan and Huan Yi advanced with eighty thousand men to the east bank of the Fei River and asked the Qin army to draw back a little so that they could cross and fight a decisive battle. Once the Qin army began to retreat it could not be stopped; Zhu Xu shouted from behind its lines, "The Qin army is beaten!", Fu Rong fell from his horse and was killed, and the Qin army broke up — "every gust of wind and cry of a crane, every bush and tree, seemed an enemy soldier". Fu Jian, struck by a stray arrow, fled north; only Murong Chui's army came through intact.

384.t: Former Qin collapses · rivals rise on every side
384.era2: Former Qin: Jianyuan 20 · Later Yan: Yanyuan 1
384.d: After the defeat at the Fei River the Former Qin disintegrated. In the 1st month Murong Chui proclaimed himself King of Yan at Xingyang (Later Yan) and led the Dingling and Wuhuan to besiege Fu Pi, who held Ye; in the 3rd month Murong Hong rose at Huayin and Murong Chong at Pingyang (Western Yan), and at the end of the year Murong Chong camped at Epang, closing in on Chang'an; in the 4th month the Qiang chief Yao Chang styled himself Wannian King of Qin north of the Wei River (Later Qin). Xie Xuan of the Eastern Jin seized the chance to march north and recovered Pengcheng, Juancheng and other places, and Huan Chong sent generals to recover Xiangyang and Weixing. In the Western Regions Lü Guang took Kucha, and more than thirty states submitted.

385.era2: Former Qin: Tai'an 1 · Later Yan: Yanyuan 2
385.d: In the 5th month Murong Chong of the Western Yan broke into Chang'an; Fu Jian fled to Mount Wujiang, was captured by Yao Chang of the Later Qin in the 7th month, and in the 8th month was strangled in a Buddhist temple at Xinping. Fu Pi abandoned Ye, went west to Jinyang and proclaimed himself emperor; the Later Yan gained Ye. In the 9th month Qifu Guoren of the Longxi Xianbei styled himself Grand Chanyu at Yuanchuan (Western Qin). Lü Guang led his western army back east, defeated Liang Xi, the Former Qin Inspector of Liang Province, at Anmi in the 9th month, and occupied Guzang (Later Liang). Xie An of the Eastern Jin died of illness in the 8th month; the northern expeditionary armies recovered Qing Province and Luoyang and reached Liyang, and Ba-Shu also returned to the Eastern Jin.

386.t: Northern Wei founded · Later Yan and Later Qin rulers proclaim themselves emperors
386.d: In the 1st month Tuoba Gui gathered the old followers of Dai at Niuchuan and became King of Dai, changing the title to King of Wei in the 4th month (Northern Wei); in the same month Murong Chui proclaimed himself emperor at Zhongshan, and Yao Chang of the Later Qin at Chang'an. More than four hundred thousand Western Yan Xianbei headed back east amid repeated internal strife, and in the 10th month Murong Yong occupied Zhangzi and proclaimed himself emperor. Fu Pi was defeated by the Western Yan and killed by the Jin army; Fu Deng took the throne at Nan'an and fought the Later Qin back and forth in eastern Long. Lü Guang styled himself Governor of Liang Province. Yang Ding, a Di, returned to Chouchi and restored the Yang regime.

389.t: Zhai Wei holds Huatai · Later Liang ruler takes the title King of Sanhe
389.d: In 387 Tuoba Gui, allied with the Later Yan, crushed Liu Xian of the Dugu, and the Northern Wei held the area of Shengle and Pingcheng; in 388 he also crushed the Kumo Xi to the north, and from then on the Khitan and the Kumo Xi were two separate peoples. In 388 Zhai Liao of the Dingling styled himself Heavenly King of Wei at Huatai (Zhai Wei), holding Dong, Chenliu and Puyang commanderies on both banks of the Yellow River. In 389 Lü Guang styled himself King of Sanhe; Qifu Gangui succeeded to the Western Qin and styled himself King of Henan. Rome and Persia partitioned Armenia in 387, Rome taking the west.

392.t: Later Yan destroys Zhai Wei · Northern Wei takes the Hetao
392.d: In 391 Tuoba Gui of the Northern Wei struck the Rouran at the Nanchuang Mountains in the north, then crossed the Yellow River and killed Liu Weichen of the Tiefu at Yueba City in a surprise attack, taking the whole of the Hetao; Weichen's son Helian Bobo fled to the Later Qin. In the 6th month of 392 Murong Chui of the Later Yan campaigned in person against Zhai Wei, crossed the river and took Huatai; Zhai Zhao fled to the Western Yan, and Zhai Wei fell. In the generation of Shelun's father the Rouran roamed north of the Gobi as subjects of the Northern Wei, and the Chile tribes lived scattered to their north.

394.t: Later Yan destroys Western Yan · end of Former Qin
394.era2: Wei: Dengguo 9 · Later Yan: Jianxing 9 · Later Qin: Huangchu 1
394.d: In 393 Yao Chang of the Later Qin died of illness and his son Yao Xing took the throne; in the 7th month of 394 Yao Xing crushed Fu Deng at Feiqiao, and Fu Deng was killed; his son Fu Chong fled to Huangzhong and proclaimed himself emperor, but in the 10th month he was killed by Qifu Gangui of the Western Qin, and the Former Qin came to an end. Murong Chui of the Later Yan attacked the Western Yan along three routes, routed Murong Yong at Taibi in the 6th month and took Zhangzi in the 8th; the Western Yan fell, and Bing Province passed to the Later Yan.

395.d: In the 5th month Murong Bao, crown prince of the Later Yan, invaded Wei with an army of eighty thousand; Tuoba Gui cleared the countryside, held his walls and drew the enemy deep, and the two armies faced each other across the Yellow River. In the 10th month, hearing a rumor that Murong Chui was dying, the Yan army withdrew, and in the 11th month it was overtaken by the Wei army at Canhe Slope, where forty or fifty thousand Yan soldiers were buried alive; the Later Yan never recovered its strength. In the Eastern Jin Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, monopolized power, while Wang Gong at Jingkou and Yin Zhongkan at Jiangling divided military command of the lower and upper Yangtze. The Roman emperor Theodosius I died and the empire was divided between his two sons, East and West; thereafter the Eastern Roman Empire corresponds to the "Daqin" of Chinese histories.

396.t: Northern Wei attacks Yan · takes Bing Province
396.d: In the 3rd month Murong Chui campaigned against the Northern Wei in person, took Pingcheng, and died of illness at Shanggu; Murong Bao took the throne. In the 8th month Tuoba Gui marched south against the Later Yan with more than four hundred thousand foot and horse; in the 9th month he took Jinyang and Bing Province passed to Wei, and in the winter he sent columns east through Jingxing to besiege Zhongshan, Ye and Xindu. Yao Xing of the Later Qin held Puban and Hedong. Lü Guang took the title Heavenly King, naming his state Great Liang (Later Liang). In the 9th month Emperor Xiaowu of the Eastern Jin was murdered by his consort Lady Zhang, and Emperor An took the throne.

397.t: Northern Wei takes Zhongshan · two Liang states split off
397.d: In the 2nd month the Wei army, after a setback in a night battle at Baisi, regrouped, and in the 3rd month Murong Bao abandoned Zhongshan and went north to Longcheng; in the 10th month the Wei army took Zhongshan, the main Later Yan forces fell back north to Liaoxi, and all of Hebei passed to the Northern Wei, except Ye, still held by Murong De. In the 1st month Tufa Wugu of the Hexi Xianbei styled himself King of Xiping (Southern Liang); in the 5th month Juqu Mengxun of the Lushui Hu made Duan Ye, the Later Liang Administrator of Jiankang, Governor of Liang Province (Northern Liang), and the Later Liang split apart. Wang Gong of the Eastern Jin rose in arms, claiming he would execute Wang Guobao, and Sima Daozi was forced to put Wang Guobao to death.

398.t: Northern Wei moves its capital to Pingcheng · Southern Yan founded
398.d: In the 1st month Murong De moved south from Ye to Huatai with forty thousand households and styled himself King of Yan (Southern Yan); in the 7th month Tuoba Gui moved his capital to Pingcheng, and in the 12th month he proclaimed himself emperor (Emperor Daowu). Troops mutinied at the Later Yan capital Longcheng; Murong Bao was killed by Lan Han, and Murong Sheng put down the revolt and took the throne. Duan Ye of the Northern Liang took Zhangye. In the Eastern Jin, Wang Gong, Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan and Yang Quanqi rose in arms again; the Northern Headquarters general Liu Laozhi turned against them and Wang Gong was killed; Huan Xuan, Yin Zhongkan and Yang Quanqi made an alliance at Xunyang and, dividing the three provinces of Jing, Jiang and Yong between them, defied the court.

399.t: Sun En rises · Southern Yan moves east · Later Qin takes Luoyang
399.d: In the 1st month the Southern Yan lost Huatai to the Northern Wei; Murong De took Qing Province to the east, killed Biqiu Hun, the Eastern Jin Inspector of Qing Province, and made Guanggu his capital. In the 10th month Yao Xing of the Later Qin took Luoyang, and most of the cities north of the Huai and Han surrendered to the Later Qin. In the 10th month Sun En, a leader of the Way of the Five Pecks of Rice, struck from the offshore islands and took Kuaiji; the eight commanderies of the Three Wu rose in answer and his following grew to several hundred thousand, but in the 12th month Liu Laozhi drove him back to the islands. In the 12th month Huan Xuan killed Yin Zhongkan and Yang Quanqi in surprise attacks and took all three provinces of Jing, Jiang and Yong.

400.t: Western Liang founded · Later Qin absorbs Western Qin
400.d: In the 1st month Murong De of the Southern Yan proclaimed himself emperor at Guanggu. In the 7th month Yao Shuode of the Later Qin attacked the Western Qin in force; Qifu Gangui was defeated and surrendered to Qin, and the Western Qin ceased to exist for a time. In the 11th month Li Gao, Administrator of Dunhuang, was acclaimed Grand Area Commander and Duke of Liang, holding Dunhuang and Jinchang (Western Liang). The Northern Wei built palaces and an ancestral temple at Pingcheng and moved more than a hundred thousand officials, commoners and assorted non-Chinese from the six provinces east of the mountains to fill the capital, allotting them land by head count.

401.t: Juqu Mengxun seizes Northern Liang · Later Liang becomes a vassal
401.d: In the 5th month Juqu Mengxun killed Duan Ye and styled himself Duke of Zhangye, and the Northern Liang passed to the Juqu clan. In the 9th month Yao Shuode of the Later Qin besieged Guzang, and Lü Long of the Later Liang submitted as a vassal; the state survived in name only. In the 6th month Sun En went north to attack Jingkou and pressed on Jiankang, but was defeated by Liu Yu, a general under Liu Laozhi, and fell back to the sea. Murong Sheng of the Later Yan was killed and Murong Xi took the throne. In the north, those standing side by side at this moment were the Northern Wei, Later Yan, Southern Yan, Later Qin, Later Liang, Southern Liang, Northern Liang and Western Liang; together with the Eastern Jin, Chouchi and the Tuyuhun, the division of the north was at its height. King Gwanggaeto of Goguryeo attacked Baekje to the south and took back the old Daifang lands. In India Chandragupta II of the Gupta dynasty conquered the Saka kings of the west; Faxian was at this time on his journey west in search of the Dharma.

402.t: Huan Xuan enters Jiankang · Battle of Chaibi
402.d: In the 1st month Sima Yuanxian issued an edict for war on Huan Xuan; Huan Xuan came down the Yangtze, the Northern Headquarters commander Liu Laozhi turned and went over to him, and in the 3rd month Huan Xuan entered Jiankang, killed Sima Yuanxian, made himself Grand Commandant and Governor of Yang Province and took over the whole government; he then stripped the Northern Headquarters of its command, and Liu Laozhi hanged himself. In the 3rd month Sun En failed in an attack on Linhai and drowned himself in the sea; his brother-in-law Lu Xun took over his remaining followers. The Northern Wei and the Later Qin fought over Hedong; in the 10th month Tuoba Gui crushed Yao Ping at Chaibi, and the Later Qin never again dared to strike east. Shelun of the Rouran crushed the Chile to the north, united the lands north of the Gobi and styled himself Qiudoufa Qaghan.

403.t: Huan Xuan usurps the Jin throne · end of Later Liang
403.d: In the 12th month Huan Xuan forced Emperor An to abdicate and proclaimed himself emperor at Jiankang, naming his state Chu (Huan Chu), and moved Emperor An to Xunyang. In the 8th month the Later Qin moved Lü Long of the Later Liang, with his clan and people, to Chang'an; the Later Liang came to an end, and Guzang was held by Wang Shang, the Later Qin Inspector of Liang Province. The Later Qin stationed Helian Bobo in Shuofang.

404.t: Liu Yu takes up arms · Huan Xuan defeated and killed
404.d: In the 2nd month Liu Yu, Liu Yi, He Wuji and others rose at Jingkou and Guangling against Huan Xuan, and in the 3rd month they broke into Jiankang; Huan Xuan fled west to Jiangling, taking Emperor An with him, was defeated at Zhengrong Islet in the 5th month and killed at Meihui Islet; in the 10th month Huan Zhen retook Jiangling. In the 10th month Lu Xun took Panyu and held Guang Province. King Gwanggaeto of Goguryeo took Liaodong from the Later Yan.

405.d: In the 2nd month Qiao Zong, an Adjutant of Yi Province, mutinied at Fucheng, killed the Inspector Mao Qu and styled himself King of Chengdu (Western Shu), acknowledging the Later Qin as his overlord. In the 3rd month Liu Yi and others took Jiangling, the remnants of the Huan clan were put down, and Emperor An was restored, with Liu Yu, a Northern Headquarters general, in control of the government. The Eastern Jin made Lu Xun Inspector of Guang Province to placate him. Murong De of the Southern Yan died and Murong Chao took the throne. Li Gao of the Western Liang moved his capital to Jiuquan.

407.t: Xia founded · Northern Yan replaces Later Yan
407.d: In 406 the Later Qin gave Guzang to Tufa Rutan of the Southern Liang, and the Southern Liang moved its capital there. In the 6th month of 407 Helian Bobo of the Tiefu Xiongnu broke with the Later Qin and styled himself Heavenly King of Great Xia (Xia), raiding north of the ridges year after year; in the 7th month Feng Ba, a commander of the Later Yan palace guard, killed the tyrant Murong Xi and enthroned Gao Yun, adopted son of Murong Bao: the Later Yan was at an end, and the regime is known to history as the Northern Yan. In his later years Emperor Daowu of the Northern Wei took Cold Food Powder and grew suspicious and murderous.

409.t: Liu Yu's northern expedition against Southern Yan
409.d: In the 4th month Liu Yu led his fleet from the Huai into the Si, crossed the Daxian Mountains, routed the Southern Yan army at Linqu in the 6th month and laid siege to Guanggu, and most of the Southern Yan commanderies and counties surrendered. In the 7th month Qifu Gangui restored his state at Yuanchuan (Western Qin). In the 10th month Emperor Daowu of the Northern Wei was killed by his second son Tuoba Shao, and his eldest son Tuoba Si put down the revolt and took the throne (Emperor Mingyuan). Gao Yun of the Northern Yan was killed by his favorites Li Ban and Tao Ren; Feng Ba put down the revolt and made himself ruler.

410.t: Fall of Southern Yan · Lu Xun strikes north
410.d: In the 2nd month the Jin army took Guanggu; Murong Chao was captured and beheaded at Jiankang, and the Southern Yan came to an end. Lu Xun and Xu Daofu took advantage of Liu Yu's northern expedition to march north from Guang Province along separate routes; in the 3rd month He Wuji was killed in battle at Yuzhang, in the 5th month Liu Yi was routed at Sangluo Islet, and Lu Xun pressed on Jiankang. Liu Yu hurried his army back and held Shitou City; unable to take it after a long attack, Lu Xun fell back to Xunyang, and in the 12th month Liu Yu crushed him at Zuoli, while sending Sun Chu and Shen Tianzi by sea to take Panyu by surprise. The Southern Liang was defeated by the Northern Liang, and Tufa Rutan fell back to Ledu.

413.d: In 411 Lu Xun was defeated and died in Jiao Province. In 412 Liu Yu killed Liu Yi, Inspector of Jing Province, in a surprise attack and installed Sima Xiuzhi at Jiangling. In the 7th month of 413 Zhu Lingshi led an army up the Outer River in a surprise attack on Chengdu; Qiao Zong fled and hanged himself, Western Shu fell, and Ba-Shu returned to the Eastern Jin. In 412 Qifu Chipan took the throne of the Western Qin and moved the capital to Fuhan; Juqu Mengxun of the Northern Liang moved his capital to Guzang and took the title King of Hexi.

414.d: In the 6th month Qifu Chipan of the Western Qin seized Ledu in a surprise attack while Tufa Rutan of the Southern Liang was away campaigning west against the Yifu; Rutan surrendered, the Southern Liang fell, and Hehuang passed to the Western Qin. The Northern Liang, the Western Qin and the Western Liang divided Hexi and Longyou among them.

416.t: Liu Yu's northern expedition · Luoyang recovered
416.d: In the 2nd month Yao Xing of the Later Qin died of illness and his son Yao Hong took the throne, while his brothers fought over the succession; Helian Bobo of Xia took Anding, Yinmi and other Later Qin territory. In the 8th month Liu Yu launched a northern expedition along five routes; Wang Zhen'e and Tan Daoji advanced from the Huai and the Fei toward Xuchang and Luoyang, and in the 10th month they took Luoyang and restored the five tombs of the Jin emperors.

417.d: In the 1st month Liu Yu led his fleet from Pengcheng along the Si and the Bian into the Yellow River; the Northern Wei shadowed and harassed him from the north bank, and Liu Yu routed the Wei cavalry with his "Crescent Formation". Wang Zhen'e led a fleet up the Wei River and in the 8th month arrived beneath the walls of Chang'an, left his boats, went ashore and crushed the Qin army; Yao Hong surrendered, and the Later Qin fell. In the 12th month Liu Yu left his son Liu Yizhen in charge of Chang'an and returned to Jiankang himself.

418.d: After Liu Yu went back east, the Jin generals in Guanzhong turned on one another: Shen Tianzi killed Wang Zhen'e, and Wang Xiu in turn killed Shen Tianzi. Helian Bobo of Xia seized the chance to strike south; in the 11th month Liu Yizhen abandoned Chang'an and withdrew east, was overtaken and routed by the Xia army at Qingni, and the Xia army took Chang'an; Bobo proclaimed himself emperor at Bashang, made Chang'an his southern seat of government, and went back to Tongwan himself. In the 12th month Liu Yu had Emperor An strangled and set up Emperor Gong.

420.t: Liu Song replaces Jin · Northern Liang destroys Western Liang
420.d: In the 6th month Liu Yu accepted the abdication of Emperor Gong of Jin and proclaimed himself emperor at Jiankang, naming his dynasty Song; the Eastern Jin was at an end, and the Southern Dynasties began. In the 7th month Juqu Mengxun of the Northern Liang feigned an attack on the Western Qin to lure Li Xin of the Western Liang into the field, routed the Western Liang army at Liaoquan, and took Jiuquan; Li Xin was killed in battle. His younger brother Li Xun fell back to hold Dunhuang, which fell the following year, and the Western Liang came to an end.

423.t: Northern Wei seizes Song's lands south of the Yellow River
423.d: In the 5th month of 422 Emperor Wu of Song, Liu Yu, died of illness; Emperor Mingyuan of the Northern Wei seized the moment of mourning to invade the south and took Huatai in the 11th month; in the 1st month of 423 he took Luoyang, and in the intercalary 4th month he took Hulao after Mao Dezu had held it for more than two hundred days. Song lost much of its land south of the Yellow River in Si, Yan and Yu provinces, keeping only Dongyang City in Qing Province and its strongholds north of the Huai. In the 11th month Emperor Mingyuan died and Emperor Taiwu, Tuoba Tao, took the throne. In 421 the Northern Liang had taken Dunhuang, and the Western Liang had come to an end.

427.d: In 425 the Xia ruler Helian Bobo died and his son Helian Chang took the throne. In 426 Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei campaigned west, and Xi Jin took Chang'an; in the 6th month of 427 Emperor Taiwu raced to Tongwan City with light cavalry, lured the Xia army out to fight and crushed it, and took Tongwan; Helian Chang fled to Shanggui. Emperor Wen of Song, Liu Yilong, put the government in order and opened the good rule of the Yuanjia era.

430.t: Yuanjia northern expedition · Wei takes Pingliang
430.d:
In the 3rd month Emperor Wen of Song sent Dao Yanzhi north with an army of fifty thousand; the Wei army withdrew of its own accord, and Song recovered the four garrisons south of the Yellow River — Luoyang, Hulao, Huatai and Qiao'ao. In the 10th month the Wei army crossed the river to counterattack, and in the 11th month it retook Luoyang and Hulao; Dao Yanzhi burned his boats, threw away his armor and fled south, and only Huatai was still held by the Song army. In the same month Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei struck west at Xia and took Pingliang, and Guanzhong and eastern Long passed wholly to the Northern Wei; Helian Ding fell back to hold Shanggui. In 428 the Northern Wei had captured the Xia ruler Helian Chang, and his younger brother Helian Ding had succeeded him.
King Jangsu of Goguryeo moved the capital to Pyongyang in 427. In the Yuanjia era of Song, Heluodan, Panpan, Pohuang and other states of the Southern Seas sent envoys with tribute one after another. The Armenian kingdom was abolished by the Sasanians in 428 and replaced by a governor.

431.t: Xia destroys Western Qin · Tuyuhun destroys Xia
431.d: In the 1st month Helian Ding took the Western Qin and killed Qifu Mumo, and the Western Qin fell; in the 6th month Helian Ding led more than a hundred thousand of his people west across the Yellow River intending to attack the Northern Liang, but halfway across he was intercepted and captured by Mugui of the Tuyuhun; Xia fell, and the Northern Wei promptly took Shanggui. In the 2nd month the Northern Wei took Huatai, and Tan Daoji of Song brought his whole army home by "counting sand as if it were grain". Juqu Mengxun of the Northern Liang declared himself a subject of the Northern Wei, and the Tuyuhun held Fuhan and Xiping.

436.d: From 432 the Northern Wei attacked the Northern Yan year after year; in the 4th month of 436 the Wei army closed in on Longcheng, Goguryeo sent tens of thousands of troops to receive Feng Hong, and Feng Hong burned his palaces and drove the people of the city east with him to Goguryeo: the Northern Yan fell, and Liaoxi passed to the Northern Wei. Emperor Wen of Song killed his famous general Tan Daoji, and when the Northern Wei heard of it they said, "Daoji is dead — the men of Wu are no longer worth fearing." The Yueban, remnants of the Northern Xiongnu, sent envoys to the Northern Wei, agreeing to attack the Rouran together. In the northeast the Yilou came to be called Wuji.

439.t: Northern Wei destroys Northern Liang · the north unified
439.d: In the 6th month Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei campaigned in person against the Northern Liang, and in the 9th month he took Guzang; Juqu Mujian surrendered, the Northern Liang fell, and the Northern Wei unified the north: the era of the Sixteen Kingdoms was over, and the confrontation of the Northern and Southern Dynasties took shape. The remnants of the Juqu clan, led by Juqu Wuhui and Juqu Anzhou, fell back to hold Dunhuang and later went west to Shanshan and Gaochang.

442.t: The Juqu hold Gaochang · Song crushes Chouchi
442.d: In 441 the Northern Wei attacked Dunhuang; Juqu Wuhui abandoned the city and went west to Shanshan, and in the 9th month of 442 he took Gaochang in a surprise attack and styled himself King of Liang (the Gaochang Northern Liang), while Dunhuang passed to the Northern Wei; Tang He, the commander at Yiwu, went over to the Northern Wei. In the 5th month the Song general Pei Fangming took Chouchi, Yang Nandang fled north to the Northern Wei, and Chouchi passed to Song, only to be taken by the Northern Wei the following year; the remnants of the Yang fell back to hold Wudu. Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei favored Daoism and suppressed Buddhism, and Kou Qianzhi's Way of the Celestial Masters flourished.

451.t: Yuanjia northern expedition · Wei army waters its horses at the Yangtze
451.d:
In the 2nd month of 450 Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei invaded the south with a hundred thousand horsemen and besieged Xuanhu for forty-two days without taking it. In the 7th month Emperor Wen of Song launched a great northern expedition; Wang Xuanmo besieged Huatai for a long time without success, and in the 10th month Emperor Taiwu crossed the river at the head of a great army to relieve it, routing Wang Xuanmo. The Wei army marched south along five routes, and in the 12th month Emperor Taiwu reached Guabu on the north bank of the Yangtze, cut a winding road up the hill and announced that he would cross the river; Jiankang was placed under martial law, and the Song provinces and commanderies of Huainan were laid waste. The same year Emperor Taiwu executed Cui Hao in the State History affair. In the 1st month of 451 Emperor Taiwu went back north, besieging Xuyi for thirty days on the way without taking it, and carried off more than fifty thousand households from Huainan; the Song provinces and commanderies north of the Yangtze lay in ruins — "towns and villages desolate, the rule of Yuanjia in decline".
In 445 the Northern Wei crushed the Tuyuhun and set up Fuhan Garrison; in 448 the Wei general Wan Dugui took Shanshan and Karasahr and advanced as far as Kucha. In 450 Juqu Anzhou destroyed Nearer Jushi and held Jiaohe.

460.t: Rouran destroys Northern Liang at Gaochang
460.d: In the 1st month of 451 the Wei army failed to take Xuyi, burned and plundered as it went home, and left scorched earth wherever it passed. In 452 Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei was murdered by the eunuch Zong Ai; Emperor Wencheng took the throne, gave the people respite, restored Buddhism and began the Yungang Grottoes. In 453 Liu Shao, crown prince of Song, murdered his father; Liu Jun, Prince of Wuling, rose, put down the revolt and took the throne (Emperor Xiaowu); in 454 Liu Yixuan, Inspector of Jing Province, rebelled and was soon defeated and killed, and Emperor Xiaowu carved Ying Province out of Jing, Xiang, Jiang and Yu provinces to weaken the upper Yangtze. In 460 the Rouran took Gaochang and killed Juqu Anzhou, ending the last of the Northern Liang, and set up Kan Bozhou as King of Gaochang. The Karasahr Garrison that the Northern Wei had set up had by this time been abolished.

466.t: Yijia rebellion · Northern Wei gains the lands north of the Huai
466.d:
In 465 the Former Deposed Emperor of Song, Liu Ziye, was killed, and Liu Yu (刘彧), Prince of Xiangdong, took the throne (Emperor Ming); in the 1st month of 466 Liu Zixun, Prince of Jin'an and Inspector of Jiang Province, proclaimed himself emperor at Xunyang with the era name Yijia, and nearly every province and commandery rose in answer, but in the 8th month the rising was put down by Emperor Ming. Rebels who feared for their lives — Xue Andu, Inspector of Xu Province, Chang Zhenqi, Administrator of Runan, and Bi Zhongjing, Inspector of Yan Province — surrendered Pengcheng, Xuanhu and Xiaqiu to Wei respectively; the Northern Wei sent Yu Yuan into Pengcheng, and Song's lands north of the Huai began to slip away.
The Hephthalites (White Huns) had by this time replaced the Kidarites and held the lands of Tokharistan.

469.t: Song loses the four provinces north of the Huai
469.d: In the 1st month of 467 the Song generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi tried to retake Pengcheng but were routed by Yu Yuan at Lüliang, and more than half their men froze to death. Murong Baiyao of the Northern Wei attacked Qing and Ji provinces, took Licheng and Liangzou in 468, and in the 1st month of 469 took Dongyang City, capturing Shen Wenxiu, the Song Inspector of Qing Province. Song's provinces of Qing, Ji, Xu and Yan, and the part of Yu Province west of the Huai, all passed to the Northern Wei, and the border between north and south was pushed to the Huai; Song kept only the émigré provinces of Qing and Ji set up around Yuzhou (today's Yuntai Mountain in Lianyungang).

475.d: In the 9th month King Jangsu of Goguryeo besieged the Baekje royal capital Hanseong at the head of thirty thousand men; the city fell in seven days, King Gaero of Baekje was killed, King Munju moved south to Ungjin, and the whole Han River basin passed to Goguryeo. In 471 Emperor Xianwen of the Northern Wei abdicated in favor of his five-year-old son Tuoba Hong (Emperor Xiaowen), and Empress Dowager Feng ruled from behind the screen. The Later Deposed Emperor of Song, Liu Yu (刘昱), was cruel; in 474 Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, rose at Xunyang and was beheaded by Xiao Daocheng, who thereby gained control of the palace army.

479.t: Xiao Daocheng replaces Song and founds Qi
479.d: In the 7th month of 477 Xiao Daocheng killed the Later Deposed Emperor of Song, set up Emperor Shun, Liu Zhun, and took sole control of the government; in the 12th month Shen Youzhi, Inspector of Jing Province, rose at Jiangling against Xiao Daocheng, but in the 1st month of 478 he failed to take Yingcheng, his followers scattered, and he hanged himself. In the 4th month of 479 Xiao Daocheng accepted the abdication and proclaimed himself emperor, naming his dynasty Qi (Southern Qi), and Song came to an end. In the Northern Wei, Empress Dowager Feng, ruling from behind the screen, introduced official salaries. In the far west the Hunnic empire broke up after the death of Attila, and the steppe north of the Black Sea and the Caspian passed to the Bulgar and Sabir tribes.

494.t: Emperor Xiaowen moves the capital to Luoyang
494.d:
In 485 the Northern Wei issued the equal-field decree, and in 486 it set up the system of the Three Elders. Empress Dowager Feng died in 490 and Emperor Xiaowen took personal control; in 493, ostensibly marching south, he led three hundred thousand foot and horse to Luoyang and, using the ceaseless autumn rains, had the court agree to move the capital; in the 10th month of 494 the capital formally moved to Luoyang, and thereafter Xianbei dress and the northern language were banned, Chinese surnames adopted and family ranks fixed. Emperor Ming of Qi, Xiao Luan, deposed and killed two emperors in 494 and took the throne himself.
In 487 Afuzhiluo of the Fufuluo tribe of the Gaoche led more than a hundred thousand tents west, broke away from the Rouran, and founded a state northwest of Nearer Jushi; Gaochang was ruled in turn by kings of the Zhang, Ma and Qu clans. In 494 Buyeo, pressed by the Wuji, came to an end when its royal house fled to Goguryeo. The Hephthalites moved south to take Gandhara, absorbing the remnants of the Kidarites; the Tuyuhun held Shanshan and Qiemo; the Pugyal of the Yarlung valley were growing stronger.

498.d: In the 8th month of 497 Emperor Xiaowen marched south against Southern Qi in person with an army of two hundred thousand, besieging Wancheng and Xinye; in the 1st month of 498 he took Xinye, in the 2nd month Fang Boyu, the Qi Administrator of Nanyang, surrendered Wancheng to Wei, and the five commanderies north of the Mian passed wholly to the Northern Wei; in the 3rd month the Wei army routed the Qi army at Dengcheng. In the 7th month Emperor Ming of Qi died, and Xiao Baojuan, the Marquis of Donghun, took the throne and slaughtered his ministers.

500.t: Shouyang goes over to Wei · Xiao Yan takes up arms
500.d: In the 1st month Pei Shuye, the Qi Inspector of Yu Province, surrendered Shouyang to Wei, and the great Huainan stronghold passed to Wei. Emperor Xiaowen had died in 499 on campaign in the south, and Emperor Xuanwu had taken the throne. In the 10th month of 500 the Marquis of Donghun killed Xiao Yi (萧懿), Director of the Department of State Affairs; in the 11th month Xiao Yi's younger brother Xiao Yan, Inspector of Yong Province, rose at Xiangyang, joined forces with Xiao Yingzhou, acting head of Jing Province, set up Xiao Baorong, Prince of Nankang, as his sovereign, and in the 12th month went down the Yangtze.

502.d: In the 3rd month of 501 Xiao Baorong took the throne at Jiangling (Emperor He); Xiao Yan's army went down the Yangtze, took Yingcheng in the 7th month and besieged Jiankang in the 9th, and in the 12th month the Marquis of Donghun was killed by his own men and Xiao Yan entered the city and took over the government. In the 4th month of 502 Xiao Yan accepted the abdication of Emperor He of Qi and proclaimed himself emperor, naming his dynasty Liang, and Qi came to an end. The Northern Wei seized the chance to invade the south, besieging Zhongli and Yiyang.

505.t: Northern Wei takes Yiyang and Hanzhong
505.d: In the 8th month of 504 Yuan Ying of the Northern Wei took Yiyang, and Liang lost the key ground of the Three Passes between the Huai and the Han. In the 1st month of 505 Xiahou Daoqian, Liang's Chief Clerk of Liang Province, surrendered Hanzhong to Wei, the Wei army occupied Nanzheng, and Hanzhong passed to the Northern Wei. In the 10th month Emperor Wu of Liang launched a great northern expedition under Xiao Hong, Prince of Linchuan, its equipment so fine and new that it was said nothing like it had been seen in a hundred years. On the Syrian frontier the Ghassanid Arab tribes became allies of the Eastern Roman Empire from 502.

507.d: In the 9th month of 506 the Liang commander-in-chief Xiao Hong fled in panic at Luokou at the first sign of the enemy, and the northern expedition failed; the same year the Northern Wei destroyed the Yang of Wuxing and set up Wuxing Garrison. Yuan Ying, Prince of Zhongshan, and Yang Dayan of the Northern Wei, flushed with victory, besieged Zhongli with several hundred thousand men and built a pontoon bridge at Shaoyang Islet in the Huai; in the 3rd month of 507 the Liang generals Wei Rui and Cao Jingzong, taking advantage of a sudden rise of the Huai, burned the bridge with fire ships; more than a hundred thousand Wei soldiers drowned or were killed, Yuan Ying fled back alone on horseback, and the Northern Wei advance south was checked.

524.t: Six Garrisons uprising · risings in Guanlong
524.d:
In 514–516 Liang built the Fushan Dam to dam the Huai and flood Shouyang; when finished the dam burst, and more than a hundred thousand people along the Huai were swept away and drowned. After the Northern Wei moved to Luoyang, the standing of the Xianbei military households of the Six Garrisons on the northern frontier collapsed; in 523 the Rouran raided, and the garrison people of Huaihuang killed their commander; in the 3rd month of the following year Poliuhan Baling of the Woye Garrison rose in arms, the other garrisons rose in answer, and Huaishuo, Wuchuan and others fell; in the 6th month Mozhe Dati, a Qiang of Qin Province, rose in arms and his son Mozhe Niansheng styled himself Son of Heaven; Hu Chen and Moqi Chounu rose at Gaoping, and Guanlong was in turmoil. Liang seized the chance to march north into Huainan.
Emperor Wu of Liang was devoted to Buddhism, and the states of the Southern Seas — Langkasuka, Dandan, Kantoli, Poli and others — sent envoys one after another; the Hephthalites were at their height, subjugating the states of the Western Regions to the east, invading India to the south, and seizing the Sogdian cities.

526.t: Surrendered Six Garrisons people rise · Liang takes Shouyang
526.d: In 525 the Northern Wei, with troops lent by Anagui of the Rouran, crushed Poliuhan Baling, and more than two hundred thousand who had surrendered were sent to Ding, Ji and Ying provinces in Hebei to be fed. In the 8th month of 525 Du Luozhou of the Rouxuan Garrison rose at Shanggu; in the 1st month of 526 Xianyu Xiuli rose in Ding Province, and when he was killed by his own general in the 8th month, Ge Rong took over his followers and in the 9th month proclaimed himself emperor, naming his state Qi. In the 11th month the Liang generals Xiahou Dan and Wei Fang took Shouyang, and Liang recovered Huainan. In 525 Aksum (in today's Ethiopia) crossed the Red Sea, destroyed Himyar and occupied Yemen.

528.d: In the 2nd month Empress Dowager Hu poisoned Emperor Xiaoming; on this pretext Erzhu Rong, chieftain of the Qihu of Xiurong, marched south from Jinyang, in the 4th month set up Emperor Xiaozhuang, and at Heyin drowned the Empress Dowager Hu and the child emperor in the Yellow River and massacred more than two thousand princes and officials — the Heyin massacre. Ge Rong absorbed Du Luozhou and in the 9th month marched south with several hundred thousand men to besiege Ye; Erzhu Rong made a surprise attack at Fukou with seven thousand picked horsemen and captured Ge Rong alive, and Hebei was pacified. In Guanlong Moqi Chounu proclaimed himself emperor, and in Qing Province Xing Gao rose with the refugees.

529.d: Emperor Wu of Liang sent Chen Qingzhi with seven thousand white-robed troops to escort Yuan Hao, Prince of Beihai of the Northern Wei, who had fled to Liang, back north; from Zhi County to Luoyang they took thirty-two cities and won all forty-seven battles, and in the 5th month they broke into Luoyang, where Yuan Hao proclaimed himself emperor and Emperor Xiaozhuang fled north. In the intercalary 6th month Erzhu Rong's great army counterattacked, Yuan Hao was defeated and died, and Chen Qingzhi's army was wiped out; he shaved his head, disguised himself as a monk and escaped home. In the 4th month Xing Gao was put down by Yuan Tianmu.

530.d: In the 4th month Erzhu Tianguang, Heba Yue and Houmochen Yue marched west and captured Moqi Chounu alive, and Guanlong was pacified.
