In the 9th month Emperor Xiaozhuang laid an ambush in the Mingguang Hall and killed Erzhu Rong with his own hand; Erzhu Zhao struck back from Jinyang and Erzhu Shilong from Huatai, and in the 12th month Erzhu Zhao broke into Luoyang, carried Emperor Xiaozhuang to Jinyang and strangled him, and set up Yuan Ye in his place; the young men of the Erzhu clan divided Bing Province, Guanlong, Xu and Yan, and Luoyang among themselves. The northern lands of the Six Garrisons were already in Rouran hands.

531.t: Gao Huan takes up arms at Xindu
531.d: In the 2nd month Erzhu Shilong deposed Yuan Ye and set up Yuan Gong (Emperor Jiemin). In the 6th month Gao Huan rose at Xindu against the Erzhu, leading the Six Garrisons people who had surrendered; in the 10th month he made Yuan Lang, Administrator of Bohai, emperor, crushed Erzhu Zhao at Guang'e, and held Hebei.

532.d: In the 1st month Gao Huan took Ye; in the intercalary 3rd month Erzhu Zhao, Erzhu Tianguang, Erzhu Dulü and Erzhu Zhongyuan attacked Ye with a combined force of two hundred thousand, and Gao Huan, with fewer than thirty thousand men drawn up in a circular formation at Mount Hanling, fought a decisive battle and crushed the Erzhu coalition. In the 4th month Gao Huan entered Luoyang, deposed Emperor Jiemin and Yuan Lang, set up Emperor Xiaowu, Yuan Xiu, and made himself Grand Chancellor; in the 7th month he occupied Jinyang and made it his headquarters. Erzhu Tianguang was captured and killed, Erzhu Zhongyuan fled to Liang, and Guanlong was under the command of Heba Yue.

534.t: Northern Wei splits into East and West
534.d:
In 533 Gao Huan destroyed Erzhu Zhao. In the 2nd month of 534 Gao Huan incited Houmochen Yue to kill Heba Yue, Grand Branch Department Director of the West of the Passes; the generals chose Yuwen Tai to take over Heba Yue's army, and in the 4th month he killed Houmochen Yue and held Guanlong. Emperor Xiaowu broke with Gao Huan and in the 7th month fled west to Chang'an to take refuge with Yuwen Tai; in the 10th month Gao Huan set up Yuan Shanjian (Emperor Xiaojing) instead and moved the capital to Ye — the Eastern Wei; in the intercalary 12th month Yuwen Tai poisoned Emperor Xiaowu, and in the 1st month of the following year he set up Yuan Baoju (Emperor Wen) — the Western Wei. The Northern Wei Inspector of Liang Province surrendered Hanzhong to Liang.
In southern Korea Geumgwan Gaya submitted to Silla in 532. At the end of the Northern Wei the Shiwei (失韦) of the Greater Khingan in the northeast first exchanged envoys with the Central Plain. Across India rulers rose to drive out the Hephthalites, who fell back to hold Kashmir and Gandhara.

537.era2: Eastern Wei: Tianping 4 · Western Wei: Datong 3
537.d: In the 1st month Gao Huan of the Eastern Wei attacked the Western Wei along three routes; Dou Tai was killed when Yuwen Tai surprised him at Xiaoguan, and Gao Huan withdrew. In the 10th month Gao Huan crossed the Yellow River with two hundred thousand men to attack the Western Wei; Yuwen Tai, with fewer than ten thousand, laid an ambush at Shayuan with his back to the river and crushed the Eastern Wei army, taking seventy thousand prisoners. The Western Wei followed up its victory by advancing east and taking Puban in Hedong; Dugu Xin recovered Luoyang, and Yingchuan, Yu Province and other places went over to the Western Wei.

538.era2: Eastern Wei: Yuanxiang 1 · Western Wei: Datong 4
538.d: In the 7th month Hou Jing, Gao Aocao and others of the Eastern Wei besieged Jinyong City at Luoyang; Yuwen Tai led an army east to relieve it, and in the 8th month there was fierce fighting around Heqiao and Mount Mang, with victories and defeats on both sides; the Eastern Wei champion Gao Aocao was killed, but in the end the Western Wei army broke and withdrew west; Luoyang, Yingchuan and other places returned to the Eastern Wei, and the Western Wei kept only Hongnong and Hedong. Hou Jing became the Eastern Wei Grand Branch Department Director of the Henan Circuit, commanding a hundred thousand troops and ruling Henan as he pleased.

543.era2: Eastern Wei: Wuding 1 · Western Wei: Datong 9
543.d: In the 2nd month Gao Zhongmi, the Eastern Wei Inspector of Northern Yu Province, surrendered Hulao to the Western Wei, and Yuwen Tai led an army to receive it; in the 3rd month he fought a great battle with Gao Huan at Mount Mang north of Luoyang. On the first day the Western Wei won a great victory and nearly captured Gao Huan; the next day the Eastern Wei counterattacked and routed the Western Wei, Yuwen Tai barely escaping with his life, and Hulao returned to the Eastern Wei. In 541 Anagui of the Rouran destroyed the Gaoche and reunited the lands north of the Gobi; Kualü of the Tuyuhun took the title Qaghan and made Fuqi City his capital. Liang set up Ya Province on Hainan Island.

546.era2: Eastern Wei: Wuding 4 · Western Wei: Datong 12
546.d: In the 9th month Gao Huan threw the whole strength of his state against the Western Wei fortress of Yubi, digging tunnels, raising earthen mounds and cutting off the Fen River; Wei Xiaokuan met every move and held firm, and in more than fifty days the Eastern Wei lost seventy thousand killed and wounded. In the 11th month Gao Huan withdrew, fell ill from grief and anger, and in the 1st month of 547 died at Jinyang.

547.t: Hou Jing breaks with Eastern Wei · Battle of Hanshan
547.era2: Eastern Wei: Wuding 5 · Western Wei: Datong 13
547.d: In the 1st month, after Gao Huan's death, Hou Jing rebelled against the Eastern Wei with thirteen provinces of Henan, surrendering first to the Western Wei and then, in the 2nd month, to Liang; Emperor Wu of Liang took him in against his ministers' objections and made him King of Henan. Wang Sizheng of the Western Wei took the opportunity to occupy Changshe in Yingchuan, and the area of Jing Province (Rangcheng) that Hou Jing had offered also passed to the Western Wei. In the 11th month a Liang army under Xiao Yuanming dammed the Si at Hanshan near Pengcheng to attack the Eastern Wei, but was routed by Murong Shaozong, and Xiao Yuanming was captured. Lý Bí of Jiao Province, who had proclaimed himself emperor in 544, was defeated by the Liang general Chen Baxian in 547.

548.era2: Eastern Wei: Wuding 6 · Western Wei: Datong 14
548.d: In the 1st month Hou Jing was defeated at Guoyang and fell back to hold the Liang city of Shouyang; when Emperor Wu of Liang negotiated peace with the Eastern Wei, Hou Jing grew suspicious and afraid, and in the 8th month he rose against Liang at Shouyang; in the 10th month, in league with Xiao Zhengde, the Liang Prince of Linhe, he crossed the Yangtze at Caishi, broke into the outer city of Jiankang and besieged Taicheng. The Eastern Wei seized the chance to recover Henan and besieged Changshe.

549.era2: Eastern Wei: Wuding 7 · Western Wei: Datong 15
549.d: In the 3rd month Hou Jing took Taicheng; Emperor Wu of Liang was held under house arrest and starved to death in the 5th month, and Hou Jing set up the crown prince Xiao Gang (Emperor Jianwen) and let his troops plunder the Three Wu. The Liang princes in the provinces held back their armies and watched, or fought one another: Xiao Yi, Prince of Xiangdong, held Jiangling, Xiao Ji, Prince of Wuling, Yi Province, Xiao Yu, Prince of Hedong, Xiang Province, and Xiao Cha, Prince of Yueyang, Xiangyang, as a vassal of the Western Wei. The Eastern Wei used the chaos to seize the provinces of Huainan and north of the Yangtze, and in the 6th month it took Changshe and captured Wang Sizheng of the Western Wei.

550.t: Northern Qi replaces Eastern Wei · Western Wei takes Handong
550.era2: Northern Qi: Tianbao 1 · Western Wei: Datong 16
550.d: In the 5th month Gao Yang, the powerful minister of the Eastern Wei, deposed Emperor Xiaojing and took the throne himself, naming his dynasty Qi (Northern Qi). Taking advantage of the chaos in Liang, the Eastern Wei and Northern Qi took all of Huainan and the land north of the Yangtze, and Guangling, Hefei and Zhongli fell one after another; Yang Zhong of the Western Wei took the Liang commanderies of Sui, Anlu and Jingling in Handong, and Xiao Yi was forced to declare himself a subject and agree with the Western Wei on Shicheng as the border. In the 4th month Xiao Yi attacked and killed Xiao Yu in Xiang Province. Triệu Quang Phục of Jiao Province recovered Longbian and styled himself King of Yue.

551.era2: Northern Qi: Tianbao 2 · Western Wei: Datong 17
551.d: Hou Jing led his army west up the Yangtze, took Ying Province and besieged Baling, but was thwarted by Wang Sengbian's stubborn defense and fell back to Jiankang; in the 8th month he deposed Emperor Jianwen, killed him in the 10th month, and in the 11th month made himself emperor, naming his state Han. Xiao Yi sent Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian down the Yangtze with an army to punish him.

552.t: Hou Jing defeated and killed · Turks destroy the Rouran
552.era2: Northern Qi: Tianbao 3 · Western Wei: Deposed Emperor 1
552.d: In the 3rd month Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian broke into Jiankang; Hou Jing fled east and in the 4th month was killed at sea by his own men, and Liang recovered Jiankang. In the 11th month Xiao Yi took the throne at Jiangling (Emperor Yuan) without returning the capital to Jiankang, stationing Wang Sengbian at Jiankang and Chen Baxian at Jingkou. In the 4th month Xiao Ji proclaimed himself emperor at Chengdu and led his army down the Yangtze; Daxi Wu of the Western Wei took Hanzhong. Northern Qi used the chaos to occupy Liyang and other key points north of the Yangtze. In the 1st month Tumen Qaghan of the Turks crushed the Rouran, Anagui killed himself, and Tumen styled himself Il Qaghan: the Turkic Qaghanate was founded.

553.era2: Northern Qi: Tianbao 4 · Western Wei: Deposed Emperor 2
553.d: Xiao Ji led his army down the Yangtze against Xiao Yi; Xiao Yi asked the Western Wei for help, and Yuwen Tai sent Yuchi Jiong south with an army by way of Jiange. In the 7th month Xiao Ji was defeated and killed at Xiakou, and in the 8th month Yuchi Jiong took Chengdu: all of Ba-Shu passed to the Western Wei, and from then on the Cuan clans of Nanzhong and the Erhai tribes were lost to the Southern Dynasties. After King Jinheung of Silla had joined Baekje in attacking Goguryeo and recovering the Han River basin in 551, in 553 he also seized the lower Han River that Baekje had gained. In India the Gupta dynasty had disintegrated and its states stood side by side; Funan was pressed by its vassal Chenla, and Dvaravati was rising on the lower Chao Phraya.

554.era2: Northern Qi: Tianbao 5 · Western Wei: Emperor Gong 1
554.d: In the 9th month Yu Jin, Yang Zhong and Yuwen Hu of the Western Wei marched south with fifty thousand men, joined forces with Xiao Cha, and in the 11th month took Jiangling; Emperor Yuan of Liang, Xiao Yi, burned 140,000 scrolls of books old and new and surrendered, and was killed in the 12th month. The Western Wei carried off more than a hundred thousand officials and townspeople of Jiangling, men and women, to the north as slaves; the commanderies of Badong west of the gorges also passed to the Western Wei. Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian held Jiankang, and the house of Liang had no ruler. King Seong of Baekje was killed in battle at Gwansanseong.

555.t: Later Liang founded · Chen Baxian kills Wang Sengbian
555.era2: Northern Qi: Tianbao 6 · Western Wei: Emperor Gong 2
555.d: In the 1st month Xiao Cha proclaimed himself emperor at Jiangling with Western Wei backing (Later Liang), holding only the land within three hundred li of Jiangling, while Xiangyang passed to the Western Wei. Northern Qi sent the captive Xiao Yuanming back south, and in the 5th month Wang Sengbian, bowing to circumstances, accepted Xiao Yuanming as emperor; in the 9th month Chen Baxian struck from Jingkou and killed Wang Sengbian, deposed Xiao Yuanming, and in the 10th month set up Xiao Fangzhi (Emperor Jing). Northern Qi seized the chance to send armies south of the Yangtze, which faced Chen Baxian at Jiankang. Wang Lin held Xiang Province, keeping his army for himself.

557.t: Northern Zhou replaces Western Wei · Chen Baxian founds Chen
557.era2: Northern Qi: Tianbao 8 · Northern Zhou: Emperor Xiaomin 1
557.d:
In the 6th month of 556 Chen Baxian crushed the Northern Qi army north of Jiankang; in the 10th month Yuwen Tai died of illness, and his nephew Yuwen Hu became regent. In the 1st month of 557 Yuwen Jue accepted the abdication of Emperor Gong of Western Wei and took the title Heavenly King of Zhou (Northern Zhou); in the 10th month Chen Baxian accepted the abdication of Emperor Jing of Liang, naming his dynasty Chen. Wang Lin, with his army in Xiang and Ying provinces, refused to serve Chen, and the following year at Ying Province he set up Xiao Zhuang as emperor of Liang, allying himself with Northern Qi.
The Bailan and the Tanguts south of the Tuyuhun and the Qiang of Fuguo in western Sichuan first appear in Northern Dynasties histories at this time; in the northeast the Wuji came to be called Mohe.

560.t: Fall of Wang Lin · Northern Zhou enters Xiang Province
560.era2: Northern Qi: Qianming 1 · Northern Zhou: Wucheng 2
560.d: In the 2nd month the Chen general Hou Tian crushed Wang Lin at Wuhu; Wang Lin and Xiao Zhuang fled to Northern Qi, and the commanderies west of Ying Province passed to Chen. The Northern Zhou seized the chance to march south; Heruo Dun broke into Xiang Province and held off the Chen army until he withdrew the following year. After Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi died in 559 the court went through repeated upheavals; Yuwen Hu of the Northern Zhou murdered Emperor Xiaomin and then poisoned Emperor Ming, and set up Emperor Wu, Yuwen Yong (560). On the steppe north of the Black Sea the Avars appeared, coming from the east.

564.t: Battles of Jinyang and Mount Mang
564.era2: Northern Qi: Heqing 3 · Northern Zhou: Baoding 4
564.d:
In the 9th month of 563 the Northern Zhou joined forces with the Turks: Yang Zhong led ten thousand foot and horse beyond the frontier to meet the hundred thousand horsemen of Muqan Qaghan, and in the 1st month of 564 they fought a decisive battle with Northern Qi beneath the walls of Jinyang, from which the Zhou army returned badly beaten. In the 10th month Yuwen Hu threw the whole strength of the state, two hundred thousand men, against Luoyang; in the 12th month Gao Changgong, Prince of Lanling of Northern Qi, broke through to the foot of Jinyong City with five hundred horsemen and raised the siege, and Duan Shao and Hulü Guang crushed the Zhou army at Mount Mang. Chen put down the regional strongmen Liu Yi, Chen Baoying and others, and Xiang Province also passed to Chen.
Istämi Qaghan of the western Turks and Sasanian Persia caught the Hephthalites between them (c. 560); the Hephthalites were destroyed, the Turks held the land north of the Oxus, and the states of Tokharistan submitted to the Turks. Silla destroyed Daegaya in 562, and all the Gaya states passed to Silla.

573.t: Taijian northern expedition · Chen recovers Huainan
573.era2: Northern Qi: Wuping 4 · Northern Zhou: Jiande 2
573.d: In 572 Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou executed Yuwen Hu, who had held power for fifteen years, and took personal control of the government; the Last Ruler of Northern Qi listened to slanderers and killed the famous general Hulü Guang. In the 3rd month of 573 Emperor Xuan of Chen ordered Wu Mingche north against Northern Qi with an army of a hundred thousand; he took Qin Commandery, Liyang and Hefei in succession, and in the 10th month took Shouyang, capturing and beheading Wang Lin; all the land of Huainan north of the Yangtze passed to Chen. In 571 Lý Phật Tử of Jiao Province had succeeded Triệu Quang Phục in holding Longbian. In the far west the Sasanians sent an army to Yemen in 570 and drove out the Aksumites; the power of the western wing of the Turks (the Western Turks) had already reached the Volga.

577.d: In the 10th month of 576 Emperor Wu of the Northern Zhou campaigned in person against Northern Qi and took Pingyang (Jinzhou); in the 12th month he crushed the relief army led by the Last Ruler of Northern Qi beneath the walls of Pingyang and went on to take Jinyang. In the 1st month of 577 the Zhou army took Ye; the Last Ruler of Northern Qi abdicated in favor of his young son and fled east, was overtaken and captured, and Northern Qi fell: the north was reunited. Gao Baoning, the Northern Qi Inspector of Ying Province, held Ying Province and refused to surrender, allying himself with the Turks; Gao Shaoyi of the Northern Qi imperial clan fled to Taspar Qaghan of the Turks and was set up as emperor of Qi. In 576 the Turks took Bosporus (Kerch) on the north shore of the Black Sea.

578.t: Battle of Lüliang · death of Emperor Wu of Zhou
578.d: Emperor Xuan of Chen took advantage of the fall of Northern Qi to contend for the land north of the Huai, and Wu Mingche besieged Pengcheng; in the 2nd month of 578 Wang Gui of the Northern Zhou cut the Qing River at Lüliang and blocked the Chen army's retreat with cart wheels joined by iron chains, and Wu Mingche's whole army was wiped out and he was captured. In the 6th month Emperor Wu of Zhou died of illness on a northern campaign against the Turks, and Emperor Xuan, Yuwen Yun, took the throne and lived in boundless dissipation.

579.d: In the 2nd month Emperor Xuan of Zhou handed the throne to his seven-year-old son Yuwen Chan (Emperor Jing) and styled himself Emperor Tianyuan. In the 9th month Wei Xiaokuan, Liang Shiyan and others of the Northern Zhou attacked Huainan, and in the 11th month they took Shouyang; Chen lost all its land north of the Yangtze, and the river became the border between north and south.

580.t: Yuchi Jiong rises · Yang Jian takes the regency
580.d: In the 5th month Emperor Xuan of Zhou died of illness, and the empress's father Yang Jian, by a forged edict, became regent as Chancellor. In the 6th month Yuchi Jiong, Superior Area Commander of Xiang Province, rose at Ye against Yang Jian, and Sima Xiaonan, Superior Area Commander of Yun Province, and Wang Qian, Superior Area Commander of Yi Province, rose in answer one after another; Yang Jian sent Wei Xiaokuan against them, and in the 8th month Ye fell and Yuchi Jiong killed himself; Yang Jian ordered Ye burned and its people moved to Anyang. Sima Xiaonan fled south to Chen, and in the 10th month Wang Qian was defeated and died; Yang Jian took control of the whole Northern Zhou state.

581.t: Yang Jian supplants the Zhou · Sui founded
581.d:
In the 2nd month of 581 Emperor Jing of Northern Zhou abdicated in favor of his chancellor Yang Jian; the Sui dynasty was founded, with the era name Kaihuang. Sui inherited the Northern Zhou lands, holding the country north of the Yellow River and the Yangtze as well as Ba and Shu; Chen of the Southern Dynasties held Jiangnan and Lingnan, with the Yangtze as the border; the Later Liang at Jiangling was a Sui vassal; Lý Phật Tử had set himself up independently in Jiaozhou; and Yingzhou was still held by Gao Baoning, a former Northern Qi general.
To the north the Turks under Ishbara Qaghan had several hundred thousand archers and ranged from the Liao Sea in the east to the Western Sea in the west: the greatest external threat to Sui. On the western frontier the Tuyuhun held Qinghai, and Gaochang, Karasahr, Kucha, Khotan and other states were subject to the Turks; in the northeast the three kingdoms of Goguryeo, Baekje and Silla stood in rivalry.
